old: Established methods are referenced where introduced. The coordinate transforms, geometric heuristics and combined selection criteria are design choices developed for this system; their equations and worked examples are derived here. Numerical examples are calculations unless explicitly identified as recorded measurements. Implementation details are available in the submitted CleanPipeline3 source, with occasional module pointers provided below.\par
new: Established methods are referenced where introduced. The coordinate transforms, geometric heuristics and combined selection criteria are design choices developed for this system. The numerical substitutions below use the configured mechanism, stored handwriting and recorded offline processing traces; their inputs and scope are collected in Appendix~\ref{app:des-real-calculations}. old: Motor torque must be assessed at operating speed, rather than from holding torque alone. With feed $F$ in mm/min, Equation~\ref{eq:des-rpm} gives the motor speed. A travel feed of 4000\,mm/min corresponds to 100\,rev/min.

With the installed 40\,mm/revolution transmission, these correspond to 60 and 22.5\,rev/min respectively, using Equation~\ref{eq:des-rpm}.

old: Calculated example: For a chosen acceleration case, $r_p=0.006366$ m, $m=0.950$ kg, $a=0.5$ m/s$^2$, $F_f=0.0373$ N and $J_{\rm rot}=10^{-5}$ kg\,m$^2$ give $T_{\rm req}=0.006366(0.0373+0.475)+10^{-5}(0.5/0.006366)=0.00405$ N\,m. The resistance and inertia are assumed; this is not the installed motor's verified torque margin.

At constant speed, only the resistance term remains. For the recorded moving mass of 0.950\,kg, assuming $F_f=\mu_fmg$ with $\mu_f=0.004$ gives approximately $0.000237$\,N\,m. This illustrative value indicates a small resistance load, but the coefficient is unmeasured and the calculation excludes acceleration. The driver starts each segment without a controlled acceleration ramp, so allowable starting rate also depends on motor current and reflected inertia. Establishing a dynamic margin requires those quantities and a matching motor characteristic, rather than the steady-state estimate alone.
new: At constant speed, Equation~\ref{eq:des-torque} reduces to $T=r_pF_f=0.006366F_f$\,N\,m for the installed pulley, with $F_f$ in newtons. A numerical load margin requires measured carriage resistance, moving mass and reflected inertia. The available record does not establish these quantities sufficiently to substitute a verified operating load. The driver starts each segment without a controlled acceleration ramp, so a holding-torque rating alone cannot establish an allowable starting rate.

old: Algorithm~\ref{alg:des-stepping} gives the major-axis form of the implemented loop. For a short illustrative command of eight $x$ steps and three $y$ steps, the initial error is four; $y$ pulses occur on iterations 2, 5 and 7. The commanded endpoint is therefore $(8,3)$, with the minor-axis movement spread along the segment. Reversing a direction changes its sign, not the interpolation rule.
new: Algorithm~\ref{alg:des-stepping} gives the major-axis form of the implemented loop. In the generated Owen file, the segment from $(17.024,239.996)$ to $(17.065,239.643)$\,mm produces signed count changes $(3,-29)$ at the configured nominal 80 microsteps/mm. For example, the $x$ increment is $\operatorname{round}(17.065\times80)-\operatorname{round}(17.024\times80)=1365-1362=3$. The $y$ axis is therefore the major axis, with initial accumulator $\lfloor29/2\rfloor=14$; the three $x$ pulses are distributed among the 29 $y$ pulses. This evaluates the generated command at the nominal scale, rather than assuming a recovered physical homing count.

new: Here $R_S$ is the carrier\textquotesingle s sense resistance and $V_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the measured reference voltage. If the reported R10 marking is confirmed as $R_S=0.10\,\Omega$, this is $V_{\rm ref}\leq1.344$\,V before considering a lower limit imposed by carrier heating. old: For unit-length descriptor $v_g$ and the normalised median reference $r_c$ for character $c$, the prior distance is $d(g,c)=1-v_g^Tr_c$. Internal consensus instead uses pairwise $L_1$ descriptor distances and chooses the medoid with the lowest total distance. These are two distinct comparisons: resemblance to a pooled character reference and resemblance to this writer's own forms. Algorithm~\ref{alg:des-profile} gives their place in the complete profile-building procedure. For a chosen descriptor dot product of 0.9, prior distance is $1-0.9=0.1$. Three variants with pairwise $L_1$ distances 0.2, 0.6 and 0.5 have summed distances 0.8, 0.7 and 1.1, so the second is the medoid; it remains an observed glyph, rather than an averaged path.
new: For unit-length descriptor $v_g$ and the normalised median reference $r_c$ for character $c$, the prior distance is $d(g,c)=1-v_g^Tr_c$. Internal consensus instead uses pairwise $L_1$ descriptor distances and chooses the medoid with the lowest total distance. These compare a pooled character reference with this writer\textquotesingle s own forms. Dylan\textquotesingle s first stored \texttt{a} variant has recorded prior distance 0.114. Recomputing the pairwise rule on all nine final stored variants gives the smallest total distance, 33.3413, for variant index 4; the other totals range from 34.4306 to 42.9091. This demonstrates the selection rule on the final pool, without treating a new descriptor calculation as the historical filtering log. Algorithm~\ref{alg:des-profile} gives its place in profile construction.

old: Here $t$ is intended text, $\widehat t$ is recognised text, $d_{\mathrm{edit}}$ is the minimum number of insertions, deletions and substitutions, using the reader error convention~\cite[PDF p.~2, Sec.~2.1]{graves2006}, and $P$ is the model probability of the selected writer.
